newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - eyes on next week's deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - eyes on next week's deals.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended Friday's quiet session unchanged to up 1/8 point as the market looked toward its first big new issue week in quite some time.
"It's really quiet here today," one trader said, adding that while some of the more actively quoted issues were up 1/8 point, aggressive bidders were few.
"Next week you have a heavy calendar and you'll probably get some institutions involved, and usually the flow picks up a little bit," the trader said.
A municipal analyst said high-grade issues ended unchanged to slightly higher, while dollar bonds ended up about 1/8 point. Activity was light, he said.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract down 1/32 at 114-25/32. The December T-bond contract closed up 5/32 at 111-9/32. The MOB spread was 112 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 1/32 at 99-12/32 to yield 6.80 percent.

Next week's competitive deals include a $713 million New Jersey Transportation Fund Authority offering, set for 1100 EDT Wednesday and a $500 million California general obligation deal slated for 1200 EDT Tuesday.
Rick Huber, a Flagship vice president and senior portfolio manager who runs a small New Jersey fund, said overall municipal supply has been scarce lately.
"Jersey of course is very thin on a normal basis, but I haven't seen anything recently, period," he said.

"Everything that we've seen is coming insured, and we have historically been value buyers so we've been passing on a lot of this insured paper. So if it comes insured we will probably pass on it again."
Reid Smith, a senior portfolio manager and principal at Vanguard who runs a California fund, said he plans to look at the California GOs.

"Usually the state GOs are coming now as current coupon-type structures, which aren't as attractive to us," he said. "We like discounts, or we like premiums, or we like anything that gives us some convexity or some performance."
Smith likes California as a credit, adding that the state is "on a definitely upward trend." He also wants uninsured paper.

"I know the past couple of times there has been some insurance available...and a lot of that was for credit reasons," Smith said. "I think everyone generally believes that they have bottomed and they are now heading out of the woods, so we'll take a look at it."
Smith expects California's deal to come "fairly rich."
"There's not a lot of California paper out there," he said, adding that while overall issuance is expected to be brisk this week and next, "not a lot of it is California."
The New Jersey and California deals are two of the 88 competitive issues totaling $2.4 billion that are scheduled for next week.
Sixty-one negotiated deals totaling $2.52 billion are expected. Leading the list is a $459 million New York City Transit Authority deal via Dillon Read & Co.

On the cash flow side, however, municipal bond funds posted only modest inflows during the latest reporting week. AMG Data Services reported $17.688 million of investor cash flowed into bond funds during that period, a market source said.
--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655
